text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos and Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic say their two countries are developing successful, substantial cooperation.
- Serbia rejoins the Community of Danube basin countries as an active and equal participant at its seventh conference in Baden, Austria.

- This year's corn production will be almost seven million tonnes, forecasts Mile Ivanovic, director of the Zemun-Polje corn institute. Statisticians and producers' association expect around five million tonnes.
- Yugoslavia imported 180,000 tonnes of sugar this year, says agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov
- Transporters in Yugoslavia and Bosnia interested in establishing links between the two countries, says transport secretary of Chamber of economy Spasoje Spasojevic.
- Yugoslav and Bosnian commissions for missing persons met for the first time in Sarajevo since the breakout of war in the former Yugoslavia.
- Voters' and complete election lists for November 3 local and federal elections to be closed Friday at midnight.
- Dragoslav Avramovic officially submits letter to Federal election commission informing it he is withdrawing from opposition coalition list Zajedno.
- Belgrade's furniture firm Ktitor will build a furniture factory in Zemun in a joint venture with German factory Bruno Steinhof. Products will be exported on the European market.
- Craftsmen and private entrepreneurs will organise a peaceful protest Wednesday October 28 over the state's crippling tax policy.
- Foreigners show interest for Yugoslav arms at international arms exhibition held in Athens early in October.
- The federal government decides to reduce sales tax for medicine - wholesale tax will go down to 8 from 10 percent and retail to 20 from 25 percent.

- Yugoslavia's gross domestic product will increase by five to six percent which is almost three times less than expected, says director of federal statistics office Milovan Zivkovic. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4305
